body:
- The F&O market works roughly as a transfer of about ₹70,000–1,00,000 crore a year from individuals to about 700 algo-using institutions. The top 10 prop firms take three-quarters of prop profits.
- After SEBI's curbs, FPI options profits fell 55% while prop profits barely moved. The Jane Street suspension and the lower expiry-day activity hit the FPI channel (JS operated partly as an FPI) more than resident prop desks, which kept their market-making edge.
- Retail's ~₹25,000 crore of annual transaction costs is a guaranteed drag before any adverse selection, and the STT share keeps rising. Even a zero-skill trader loses money with certainty.

`insight:india-mb-starting-pe` · confidence: verified

Across 27 Indian winner windows, 17 began at trailing P/E ≤15 (Bajaj Finance 9, Astral 8, Eicher 13, Balkrishna ~2, APL Apollo 5, Deepak 8.5, Tata Elxsi 5, KPIT 8.5, Cochin 5.5, Mazagon 7, HAL 6, Avanti 13, Caplin 12.5, BSE 14, Garware 5, Alkyl 8, BEL 13); their median price multiple was ~266x. Three began at ≥35x (Dixon 40, Kaynes 104, Trent 155, where Trent's EPS was COVID-depressed); their median was ~19x. Two boom-time IPOs at 84x and 214x (Waaree, Premier) tripled EPS and still trade below their first close. Most low-P/E starts were not obscure: they were well-known companies in a panic (Mar 2009, Mar 2020) or companies misclassified as commodity businesses (Balkrishna, APL Apollo, Garware, Avanti). Practical rule for screening: the twin engine needs a low starting multiple. A great business bought at 100x+ has spent the multiple engine, and its return is capped at EPS growth minus de-rating. Caveat: survivorship bias. These are winners picked with hindsight, and many low-P/E stocks stayed cheap or failed (see case_study:suzlon, case_study:capital-goods-2007).

Links: `insight:twin-engine` (part_of), `case_study:waaree-premier-energies-2024-2026` (about), `case_study:kaynes-technology-2022-2026` (about), `case_study:balkrishna-industries-2009-2024` (about), `case_study:capital-goods-2007` (contradicts)

body:
**Hidden trap: PC Jeweller's growth, profits and low P/E** (`case_study:hidden-trap-pc-jeweller-inventory`, verified). THE GOOD NUMBER: PC Jeweller grew sales and profits fast, opened stores and traded at a fraction of Titan's P/E, so it looked like 'Titan at a discount'; it peaked ~Rs 600 (Jan 2018, pre-split). WHY IT LIED: inventory and export receivables (largely to the UAE) rose much faster than sales and CFO stayed weak or negative for years despite reported profits, funded by gold-metal loans and bank working capital. The reported profit depended on receivables that later proved hard to collect. In 2018 the promoter 'gifted' shares to family off-market, a buyback was announced and then withdrawn (-43% in a week); 2021-22 the company defaulted on ~Rs 3,400 cr of bank loans. CONTRAST WITH TITAN: Titan's negative-CFO years came from gold inventory in its own stores with single-digit debtor days and a clean group; PC Jeweller's came from export receivables to counterparties outside India plus governance events. Same flag, different content. TEST: inventory and receivable days by segment (domestic retail vs export); who owes the money; does the discount to the leader reflect worse economics. LESSON: 'cheap versus the leader' is often the market correctly pricing lower-quality earnings.

**Hidden trap: Ricoh India's MNC parent and revenue surge** (`case_study:hidden-trap-ricoh-india-mnc-growth`, verified). THE GOOD NUMBER: an Indian subsidiary of Japan's Ricoh, audited by a Big-4 affiliate, growing revenue much faster than its parent after moving into services contracts; the stock went from ~Rs 100 to above Rs 1,000 in 2013-15. Investors took MNC parentage as a governance guarantee. WHY IT LIED: a PwC forensic audit found unsupported out-of-books entries; in Q1 FY16 Rs 66.7 cr of them turned a Rs 64 cr loss into a Rs 2.7 cr profit; the FY16 loss was later estimated at ~Rs 1,118-1,123 cr; reports suggest the fraud began in FY14. Shares were suspended; minority holders got little after the NCLT recapitalisation. TELLS: (1) receivables and unbilled revenue rose faster than revenue (Beneish DSRI); (2) the subsidiary's growth was far above the parent and peers in a slow-growing hardware/services market; (3) Q2 FY16 results were delayed and the auditor raised concerns; (4) a ~26% free float made the run easy. TEST: receivable + unbilled days trend; ask why a subsidiary grows 3-5x faster than its parent; treat delayed results as a disqualifier until explained. LESSON: parentage is not an audit; local management incentives can diverge from the parent's.

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:ASIANPAINT:q3fy27-standalone-opm-20pct-plus`
- **Method:** sector cycle/lead indicator · **P(ours)** 0.45 · **P(base)** 0.55 · resolve by 2027-02-28
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 call (Nov-2026): Q2 'a little bit of a soft quarter' on mix; H1 PBDIT margin 19.6% ('higher range of the overall band'); H1 volume ~8%, value ~16% (price increases). MD Amit Syngle: for the year 'we should be able to maintain the band… 18% to 20%' via price calibration, cost-excellence programme and VAE in-house intermediates. Screener standalone OPM: Sep-25 18%, Dec-25 21%, Mar-26 21%, Jun-26 22%, Sep-26 17%.
- **Why our number differs from base:** Q3 is seasonally the strongest margin quarter and price hikes are flowing, but input inflation is the highest in years and the full-year band (18–20%) with H1 at 19.6% implies H2 near 19%. 20%+ in Q3 needs a strong mix.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Seasonality base: Asian Paints' Dec quarter standalone OPM has been ≥20% in roughly half to 60% of recent years.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if Q3 FY27 standalone Operating Profit ÷ Sales from screener.in (standalone view) ≥20.0%; company-reported standalone PBDIT margin used as tiebreak if screener is unavailable.
- **Resolution source:** screener.in Asian Paints standalone quarterly; company Q3 FY27 press release

- **Deciles** (EPS SUE): test 63d T−B +3.59% (t 2.8); top decile vs controls +2.16%. Not sharper than quintiles.
- **Revenue SUE** is weaker: test 63d T−B +2.06% (CI −0.10 to +4.08, t 1.9); its announcement reaction is about half of EPS's.
  The market drifts on profits, not sales surprises.
- **Next-day OPEN entry:** test 63d T−B +3.77% (t 3.6), top vs controls +1.55% (t 1.97). Open-entry returns include the
  entry-day move, and all events lag controls by −0.6% on this basis (a day-1 reversal), so close entry is the cleaner rule.
- **Skew.** Event-level, test, 63d: top-quintile *mean* excess +2.2% but *median* −1.0%, hit rate 47%. That median is
  mechanical in part: each stock is compared with the equal-weight mean of ~116 stocks, and the median of *all* events is
  −2.6% (hit 43%). Relative to that, the top quintile is +1.6 pp better at the median. Per-quarter *median* T−B is still
  +3.2% (test, t 2.6), and 1%/99% winsorised T−B is +4.1% (t 4.5). **The drift is broad-based, not three outliers.**
- **Basket size (test, 63d, random draws from each quarter's top quintile, 2,000 trials):** 10 names → 4-year average
  excess p5 −0.45% / median +2.34% / p95 +5.07%, below the 1% cost line 21% of the time; 15 names → p5 +0.33%, 14%;
  30 names → p5 +1.13%, 3%. You need ~30 names a quarter to collect the average reliably.
- **Mcap < ₹1,000 cr vs ≥ ₹1,000 cr (test):** top vs controls +0.36% (t 0.2) vs **+2.74% (t 3.9)**. In the test period the
  long-only effect lives in ₹1,000–50,000 cr, not in the smallest and least liquid names (train was the reverse: +4.2% vs
  +1.3%).
- **Top quintile with a positive announcement-window return** (test): +3.32% vs controls (t 4.0). With a non-positive
  reaction: +1.16% (t 1.05). This is a candidate "confirmed beat" filter for a future pre-registered test.
- **By year (63d T−B):** 2018 +2.3%, 2019 +6.9%, 2020 +7.6%, 2021 +2.5%, 2022 +3.5%, 2023 +7.9%, 2024 +4.6%, **2025 +0.9%**.
  Test quarters Dec-24 → Jun-25 were roughly 0 (−0.1, −1.9, +0.8%) and Sep-25 rebounded to +4.6%. That could be decay or
  noise. Watch it, and re-run with 2026 data.
- Per-quarter test T−B was positive in 13 of 16 quarters (negative: quarters ended Mar-22 −5.4%, Dec-24 −0.1%, Mar-25 −1.9%;
  see `india_pead_outputs/robust.json`). Train: 14 of 16 positive.

body:
- **A. Late cuts.** A target lowered in the final quarter before its deadline is scored on outcome, not as "withdrawn". "Withdrawn" (-0.5) requires an explicit, explained cut at least two quarters before the deadline (KEC FY27 revenue 12-15% -> 8-10% in Nov-26 qualifies; KEC FY26 margin 8% -> 7-7.5% in Jan-26 does not).
- **B. Ceilings and expansions.** For ceiling targets (interest %, debt, NWC days): delivered if at or below target, partly if the overshoot is <=5%, missed beyond. Margin-expansion targets are scored on the expansion promised in bp from the stated base, not on the margin level, because "89% of an 8% target" otherwise passes a +10 bp result as "partly".
- **C. Adjusted metrics.** When a target is met only on a company-adjusted basis (KPIL standalone PBT 5.9% adjusted vs 4.9% reported), score it delivered but keep it single-source, and show both numbers in `evidence`.
- **D. Silent restatements that are later beaten** (KPIL order inflow 26-28k -> "25k+" -> delivered 26k+) do not change the status, but are logged in `evidence` and counted in the narrative as a candour flag.

body:
- Equity E: StockholdersEquity → StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest.
- EBIT: OperatingIncomeLoss → (pre-tax income from continuing ops [IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxes…
  variants] + interest expense).
- Interest expense I: InterestExpense → InterestExpenseDebt → InterestAndDebtExpense → InterestExpenseNet? no (not used) →
  InterestPaidNet / InterestPaid (cash, last resort).
- Short-term debt STD: DebtCurrent if tagged; else max(LongTermDebtCurrent, LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligationsCurrent)
  + (ShortTermBorrowings, or if absent CommercialPaper + LinesOfCreditCurrent + ShortTermBankLoansAndNotesPayable).
  None tagged ⇒ 0 (a balance sheet without a short-term debt line has none).
- Total debt TD: STD + noncurrent debt (LongTermDebtNoncurrent → LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations →
  (LongTermDebt − current portion)). None tagged ⇒ 0.
- Cash C: CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue → CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents → Cash.
- CFO: NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities → …ContinuingOperations. Capex: PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment
  → PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets (missing ⇒ 0, counted). FCF = CFO − capex.
- Dividends D: PaymentsOfDividends → PaymentsOfDividendsCommonStock (missing ⇒ 0). Buybacks B:
  PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock → PaymentsForRepurchaseOfEquity (missing ⇒ 0). Treasury: TreasuryStockValue.
- Scaling sanity: any balance-sheet/flow input with |x| > 5 × total assets ⇒ that firm's dependent flags = unknown.
- A flag is **unknown** when its required inputs are missing; it is then excluded from that flag's statistics
  (denominator = firms where the flag is known). Coverage per flag is reported.

*As of 22-Nov-2026. Research, not investment advice. This compares how reliably managements' own forward statements came true, to build a sector base rate and test whether credibility predicts future delivery. It is not a stock ranking and carries no buy/sell view.*

**Roadmap:** stage 3 (is promise credibility a signal?) + stage 7 (rule-generated, dated, scoreable calls). This is the third sector of the credibility-generated forward-call test, and the **first US sector**, after auto components (16 calls) and IT mid-caps (11). **Unlocks:** 11 more calls under the *same* rule, resolving Mar–Jul 2027. 8 of them are machine-resolvable from SEC data (5 structured XBRL, 3 assisted 8-K scans), so the method's Brier(ours) vs Brier(base) can be measured across 38 calls in two markets. Graco, Middleby and Donaldson were not used: Graco guides almost nothing numeric, Middleby is mid-spin-off, and Donaldson's July fiscal year resolves after Jul-2027.

Inputs: `US-WTS.md`, `US-AOS.md`, `US-SSD.md`, `US-LECO.md` (last 6 calls each, Jul-2025 to Nov-2026). Scripts: `scripts_us_industrials/` (`promises_US-*.py` ledgers → `build_seed.py` (the IT/auto scorer; only the tags, the calendar-year label and the category map change) → `make_seed.py` (medians, SAC, base rates; writes `us_summary.json`; same constants and rule) → `make_calls.py` (calls + specs) → `make_md.py`). Seeds: `memdb/seeds/2026-11-22_promises_us_industrials.json` (82 promises, 4 analyses, 1 insight) and `memdb/seeds/2026-11-22_paper_calls_credibility_us.json` (11 theses). Pipeline: v1.3 US vocabulary (`tools/promise_tracker/pipeline/README.md`). Scoreboard: `sec_fact` now also resolves `op_margin_pct` and `capex`.
